title: FIR filter lab (DSP in hardware)
summary: A digital filter made of one hardware multiplier: up to 64 taps, 1.5 million samples per second, results equal to the math to the last bit. Design low-pass, high-pass or band-pass filters in Python, feed them sound or the built-in sine and noise generator, and measure their frequency response.
parts: nothing: everything happens inside the FPGA
tested: the self-test passed 8 of 8 checks on the real board (October 2026), with nothing connected: 900 random samples equal to the integer math, 1.471 million samples per second at 63 taps.
